system.description:
A plasma drive does more than move a ship. It also provides power to all of a ship’s other systems—the vessel’s fiery heart.

The STC standard drive for transports, compact but underpowered.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports.

The STC standard drive for transports has been extended to provide additional power in exchange for less available space.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports.

The STC standard drive for escort-grade warships.

Appropriate Hull Types: Raiders, Frigates.

The STC standard drive for smaller capital-grade warships.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers.

The STC standard drive for cruiser-grade warships.

Appropriate Hull Types: Cruisers.

The warp drive rips a vessel from the material world and hurls it into the warp, allowing it to cross vast distances in a heartbeat, but exposing it to the dangers of the immaterium.

Allows the vessel to enter and remain in the immaterium.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

Allows the vessel to enter and remain in the immaterium.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

A starship’s Geller Field creates a bubble of reality around the vessel when it traverses the warp, protecting it from the dangers that lurk there.

Protects the vessel from the myriad dangers of the Immaterium.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

The entire hull of the vessel is covered with silver, hand-inscribed hexagramic wards. These reinforce a Geller Field projected from a 50 metre statue of an Imperial Saint, located just fore of the bridge.

Shield of Faith: Any Navigation Tests to pilot the ship through the warp gain a +10 bonus. When rolling on Table 7-4: Warp Travel Encounters (see page 186), the GM rolls twice and allows the Navigator to chose which result is applied.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

Void shields create barriers of energy around a starship to protect it from stellar debris and incoming fire.

A single double-layered void shield. Provides 1 Void Shield.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

Twin, multiple-layered void shields. Provides 2 Void Shields.

Appropriate Hull Types: Cruisers.

The bridge is the starship’s brain, where the captain commands the vessel and directs its every action.

A holdover from the ship’s Navy days, this bridge was laid out and equipped with combat in mind.

Damage Control Station: As long as the bridge remains undamaged, all Tech-Use Tests to repair the ship gain +10.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

A holdover from the ship’s Navy days, this bridge was laid out and equipped with combat in mind.

Damage Control Station: As long as the bridge remains undamaged, all Tech-Use Tests to repair the ship gain +10.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

This bridge has been modified to give the ship’s master greater control over his vessel.

Enhanced Cogitator Relays: As long as the bridge remains undamaged, all Command Tests made by the captain gain +5 and all Ballistic Skill Tests to fire shipboard weapons gain +5. If this Component ever suffers a Critical Hit, it becomes unpowered on a 1d10 roll of 3 or higher.

Appropriate Hull Types: Raiders, Frigates.

This bridge has been modified to give the ship’s master greater control over his vessel.

Enhanced Cogitator Relays: As long as the bridge remains undamaged, all Command Tests made by the captain gain +5 and all Ballistic Skill Tests to fire shipboard weapons gain +5. If this Component ever suffers a Critical Hit, it becomes unpowered on a 1d10 roll of 3 or higher.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

This bridge has a station equipped with cogitator-servitors and a hololithic projector, given over to quickly loading and unloading cargo.

Organised: When working towards a Trade objective, the Explorers earn an additional 50 Achievement Points towards completing that objective.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports.

The bridges of warships are often reinforced with additional armour plating, to ensure the survival of their occupants.

Reinforced Armour: If this Component takes a Critical Hit or becomes damaged or unpowered, roll 1d10. On a 4 or higher, the component is unharmed.

Appropriate Hull Types: Raiders, Frigates.

The bridges of warships are often reinforced with additional armour plating, to ensure the survival of their occupants.

Reinforced Armour: If this Component takes a Critical Hit or becomes damaged or unpowered, roll 1d10. On a 4 or higher, the component is unharmed.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

The bridge of a ship of the line is designed with one goal in mind—winning battles.

Master Plotting Table: All Piloting and Navigation tests by crew on the Bridge gain +5.

Improved Fire Direction: All Ballistic Skill Tests to fire shipboard weapons gain +10.

Appropriate Hull Types: Cruisers.

Life sustainers fill a vital role, providing a ship with clean air and water.

The life-support system was designed for reliability and does little to remove the stink of oil and warp engine discharge.

Stale Air: Increase all Morale loss by 1.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

The life-support system was designed for reliability and does little to remove the stink of oil and warp engine discharge.

Stale Air: Increase all Morale loss by 1.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

name: Vitae Pattern Life Sustainer (Transports, Raiders, Frigates)

system.description:
This life sustainer is of STC origins, and is in common use in the Calixis Sector.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

Even the lowliest crew require bunks and mess-halls to live in.

The masters of this vessel have done little to improve the quarters left from this ship’s Navy days.

Cramped: Decrease Morale permanently by 2.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

The masters of this vessel have done little to improve the quarters left from this ship’s Navy days.

Cramped: Decrease Morale permanently by 2.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

Standard living quarters for the voidsmen of a long-distance trader.

Appropriate Hull Types: Transports, Raiders, Frigates.

Standard living quarters for the voidsmen of a long-distance trader.

Appropriate Hull Types: Light Cruisers, Cruisers.

The starship’s eyes, allowing it to ‘see’ space far beyond the range of normal eyesight.

The Imperial Navy’s standard sensor array.

External: This Component does not require hull space. Although it is external, it can only be destroyed or damaged by a Critical Hit.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

A modified version of the Imperial Navy’s standard sensor array, with boosted wideband gain.

External: This Component does not require hull space. Although it is external, it can only be destroyed or damaged by a Critical Hit.

Sensitive: Increased power draw provides a +5 bonus to the ship’s Detection.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

The sensors of this ship have been optimised for navigation, at the expense of the sensor’s other uses.

External: This Component does not require hull space. Although it is external, it can only be destroyed or damaged by a Critical Hit.

Stellar Detection: Mapping protocols provide a +5 bonus to Manoeuvre Tests to avoid celestial phenomena, but subtracts –2 from the ship’s Detection.

Long Distance Scan: When working toward an Exploration objective, the players earn an additional 50 Achievement Points toward completing that objective.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.

These, quite simply, are the some of the best sensors created by the Adeptus Mechanicus, and are reserved for their own ships and Imperial Naval scout vessels.

External: This Component does not require hull space. Although it is external, it can only be destroyed or damaged by a Critical Hit.

Eye of the Omnissiah: The exceptional sensitivity of the array grants +10 to the ship’s Detection.

Appropriate Hull Types: All Ships.
